Do you work or are you a student?.a: I'm a full-time student at the moment. I'm in my third year of a business degree, so most of my week revolves around lectures and group projects. That said, I also do a bit of freelance translation at weekends, which helps me cover my living costs and gives me a taste of real working life.
vocab: trang trải chi phí sinh hoạt

What subject did you enjoy most at schoo.a: Without a doubt, it was geography. I think it was because it combined so many things I was curious about, from climate and landscapes to how people actually live in different parts of the world. Our teacher used to bring in maps and photos from her own travels, which really brought the subject to life.
vocab: chắc chắn, không nghi ngờ gì
làm cho điều gì trở nên sinh động

Do you prefer studying alone or with oth.a: Well, it depends on what I'm doing. When I need to memorise things or write an essay, I definitely prefer working on my own because I can concentrate better. But when I'm revising for exams, studying in a small group is really useful, since we can quiz each other and fill in the gaps in our knowledge.
vocab: đố nhau, kiểm tra lẫn nhau
lấp đầy những lỗ hổng (kiến thức)

Describe a teacher who has had a strong.a:
I'd like to talk about Mr Hai, who was my literature teacher in high school. He taught us Vietnamese literature for three years, from grade ten to grade twelve, and I have to say he completely changed the way I looked at the subject.

Before I joined his class, I thought literature was just about learning model essays by heart and repeating them in exams. Mr Hai, however, had a very different approach. He was quite a quiet man, but he had a dry sense of humour and an incredible passion for books. Instead of giving us the answers, he would ask us open-ended questions and let us argue with each other. Sometimes he even played the devil's advocate on purpose, just to see whether we could defend our opinions.

What I remember most clearly is one afternoon when I handed in an essay that I'd basically copied from a guidebook. He didn't scold me in front of the class. Instead, he asked me to stay behind and told me, quite gently, that he wanted to hear my voice, not someone else's. I felt really embarrassed at the time, but that conversation was a real turning point for me.

The reason he influenced me so much is that he taught me to think for myself. From then on, I started reading more widely and writing what I genuinely believed, even if it wasn't the 'safe' answer. That habit has stayed with me ever since, and it has helped me enormously at university, where critical thinking is valued far more than memorisation. Looking back, I'm incredibly grateful that I ended up in his class.
vocab: khiếu hài hước kiểu tỉnh bơ
cố tình phản biện để thử thách lập luận

Should university education be free for.a: I think it's a very appealing idea in principle, because it would give talented young people from poorer backgrounds an equal shot at success. In countries like Germany, free tuition seems to work reasonably well. However, I'm not entirely convinced it's realistic everywhere. Universities are expensive to run, so if students don't pay, taxpayers have to foot the bill, and that money might be needed for schools or hospitals. Perhaps a fairer compromise would be generous scholarships and low-interest loans, so that cost is never the only thing standing between a capable student and a degree.
vocab: một giải pháp dung hòa công bằng hơn

How has technology changed the way stude.a: Quite dramatically, I'd say. The most obvious change is access to information: students no longer have to rely solely on textbooks, because they can watch lectures from top universities or look up almost anything in seconds. Online platforms also let people learn at their own pace, which is great for those who need extra time. On the other hand, there's a downside. Many students get easily distracted by notifications, and some rely on AI tools to do their thinking for them. So technology is a powerful tool, but it really depends on whether students use it wisely.
vocab: học theo tốc độ của riêng mình

What makes a good teacher, in your opini.a: For me, the most important quality is genuine enthusiasm for the subject, because passion tends to be contagious. If a teacher clearly loves what they're teaching, students are far more likely to engage. Beyond that, I think good teachers are patient and can explain difficult ideas in a simple way. A teacher I had at school, for instance, would always use everyday examples to explain abstract concepts in physics. Of course, subject knowledge matters too, but I'd argue that being able to connect with students on a personal level is what really sets great teachers apart.
vocab: connect with someone on a personal level
gắn kết với ai ở mức độ cá nhân
làm ai nổi bật, khác biệt

How often do you use your mobile phone?.a: Honestly, far more than I should. It's usually the first thing I check in the morning and the last thing I look at before bed. I use it for everything, from messaging friends to paying for coffee. Recently, though, I've been trying to cut down on screen time by switching it to silent mode when I'm studying.
vocab: thời gian dùng thiết bị điện tử

Which apps do you use most every day?.a: I'd say the ones I use most are Zalo and Messenger, because that's how I keep in touch with family and friends. Apart from that, I spend a fair amount of time on a language-learning app, since I try to do a short lesson every day to keep my streak going. And of course, I check Google Maps whenever I'm heading somewhere new.
vocab: duy trì chuỗi ngày liên tục

Is there any technology you could not li.a: I'd have to say my laptop. I know it sounds a bit dramatic, but almost all of my coursework, my notes and even my part-time work are on it. A few months ago it broke down for three days, and I felt completely lost. That experience made me realise just how dependent I've become on it.
vocab: nghe có vẻ hơi phóng đại

Describe a piece of technology that you.a:
The piece of technology I want to talk about is my pair of noise-cancelling headphones. They might sound like a luxury, but honestly, they've become one of the most useful things I own.

I started using them about two years ago, when I moved into a shared flat near my university. The flat was on a busy street, and there was constant noise from motorbikes, street vendors and, to be honest, my flatmates as well. I was finding it almost impossible to focus on my assignments, so after a lot of research, I decided to save up and buy a decent pair. They weren't cheap, but I thought of it as an investment.

These days I use them in all sorts of situations. When I'm studying, I switch on the noise-cancelling mode and listen to some instrumental music, and it's amazing how quickly I can get into a state of deep concentration. I also wear them on long bus journeys, so I can listen to podcasts or English lessons without being bothered by the traffic. And when I need a break, they're perfect for unwinding with my favourite albums.

The main reason they're so useful to me is that they give me control over my environment. Before I had them, I was easily distracted and often stressed, but now I can create my own quiet space wherever I am. My grades actually improved in the semester after I bought them, and I don't think that's a coincidence. Of course, I try not to wear them all the time, because I don't want to shut out the world completely, but overall they've made a huge difference to my productivity and my peace of mind.
vocab: trạng thái tập trung cao độ

Do you think people rely too much on tec.a: To some extent, yes. Many people can't navigate without a map app or remember a single phone number, which suggests we've handed over some basic skills to our devices. I also think constant reliance on smartphones can damage our attention spans. Having said that, I wouldn't call all dependence negative. Technology lets doctors diagnose diseases earlier and allows families to stay connected across continents. So the problem isn't really technology itself, but the lack of balance. If we use it as a tool rather than a crutch, I think the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks.
vocab: ở một mức độ nào đó
khả năng duy trì sự chú ý

How might artificial intelligence change.a: I think AI is likely to reshape the job market quite significantly. Repetitive tasks, such as data entry or basic customer service, are already being automated, so some of those roles may disappear. On the other hand, new jobs will probably emerge, like people who train, monitor or audit AI systems. Personally, I believe the biggest change will be within existing jobs rather than jobs vanishing altogether. A lawyer or a designer, for example, might use AI to handle routine work and focus on more creative or strategic tasks. The real challenge is making sure workers have the chance to retrain.
vocab: định hình lại thị trường lao động
công việc lặp đi lặp lại

Should children be allowed to use smartp.a: I think it depends largely on the child's age and how the phone is used. For young children, I'd say it's better to delay owning a smartphone, because they can easily become addicted to games or exposed to inappropriate content. For teenagers, though, a phone can be genuinely useful, both for safety and for learning. My younger cousin, for instance, uses hers to look up homework questions and contact her parents. So rather than a complete ban, I'd favour clear rules, like screen-time limits and parental controls, so children learn to use technology responsibly.
vocab: tính năng kiểm soát của phụ huynh

Is there much pollution where you live?.a: Unfortunately, yes. I live in Hanoi, and air pollution has become a serious problem, especially in winter, when the smog can be quite thick. On bad days, I check an air-quality app before going out and wear a mask. Noise pollution is also an issue, because the streets are packed with motorbikes from early morning until late at night.

Do you do anything to protect the enviro.a: I try to do my bit, although I'm far from perfect. For example, I always carry a reusable water bottle and a cloth bag, so I don't need to buy plastic ones. I also separate my rubbish at home. They're small steps, but I think if enough people make these changes, they can really add up.
vocab: cộng dồn lại thành đáng kể

Do you prefer the countryside or the cit.a: At this stage of my life, I'd probably choose the city. There are far more job opportunities, and I love having cafés, cinemas and bookshops on my doorstep. That said, whenever I visit my grandparents in the countryside, I really appreciate the fresh air and the slower pace of life. Maybe I'll move somewhere quieter when I'm older.
vocab: at this stage of my life
ở giai đoạn này của cuộc đời

Describe a natural place you have visite.a:
The place I'd like to describe is Ha Long Bay, in the north-east of Vietnam. It's famous for its thousands of limestone islands rising out of emerald-green water, and it's a UNESCO World Heritage Site, so I'm sure many people have heard of it.

I went there about two summers ago with my family. We'd been planning the trip for months, because it was the first time all of us, including my grandparents, could take time off together. We booked a small boat tour and spent a night on the bay, which turned out to be the highlight of the whole holiday.

During the day, we sailed between the islands, stopped to explore a huge cave full of stalactites, and went kayaking through narrow channels between the rocks. My younger brother and I also tried swimming off the side of the boat, although the water was colder than I expected. In the evening, we sat on the deck, ate fresh seafood and watched the sun go down behind the islands.

The reason it impressed me so much is the sheer scale and beauty of the landscape. Photos really don't do it justice. When you're actually there, surrounded by those towering rocks and complete silence, you feel incredibly small, in a good way. I also remember waking up early the next morning, when there was mist over the water, and it looked almost magical. At the same time, I noticed some plastic floating near the shore, which made me realise how fragile places like this are. So it left me with a sense of wonder, but also a feeling that we need to take better care of them.
vocab: điểm nhấn, phần đáng nhớ nhất
không lột tả hết vẻ đẹp
cảm giác kinh ngạc, thán phục

What are the biggest environmental probl.a: In Vietnam, I'd say the most pressing issue is air pollution in big cities like Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, mainly caused by traffic, construction and industry. Another major problem is plastic waste, which ends up in rivers and eventually the ocean. And of course, as a country with a long coastline, we're particularly vulnerable to climate change. The Mekong Delta, for instance, is already suffering from rising sea levels and saltwater intrusion, which threatens farmers' livelihoods. These problems are interconnected, so I think they need to be tackled together rather than one at a time.

Who should be responsible for protecting.a: I'd argue it has to be a shared responsibility, but governments should take the lead. The truth is that individual actions, like recycling or using less plastic, are important, yet they can only achieve so much. The biggest sources of pollution are usually industries and energy systems, and only governments have the power to regulate them, for example by introducing carbon taxes or investing in public transport. At the same time, policies only work if people actually support them. So ideally, governments set the rules and provide the infrastructure, while individuals change their everyday habits.
vocab: chỉ đạt được đến một mức nhất định

Will renewable energy replace fossil fue.a: I think it will, eventually, but probably not as quickly as many people hope. Solar and wind power have become much cheaper over the last decade, and in some countries they're already the cheapest source of new electricity. However, there are still challenges, such as storing energy for when the sun isn't shining. Many economies are also heavily dependent on coal and oil, so the transition will take time and money. My guess is that fossil fuels will gradually be phased out over the next few decades rather than disappearing overnight.
vocab: chỉ sau một đêm, ngay lập tức

What kind of job would you like to have.a: Ideally, I'd love to work in marketing, preferably for an international company. I've always been interested in why people buy certain things, and marketing seems like the perfect mix of creativity and analysis. I did a short internship at an agency last summer, and I really enjoyed brainstorming campaign ideas with the team.
vocab: sự kết hợp hoàn hảo giữa
động não, cùng nghĩ ý tưởng

Would you prefer to work from home or in.a: I think I'd go for a mix of both. Working from home saves a lot of commuting time and lets me focus on tasks that need deep concentration. But I'd miss the social side of office life, like chatting with colleagues over lunch. Also, I find it easier to switch off at the end of the day when work and home are separate.
vocab: ngắt kết nối, thôi nghĩ về công việc

What do you usually do after work or stu.a: It varies, but I usually try to do something active to clear my head. Three evenings a week, I go jogging in the park near my house. On other days, I'll cook dinner, catch up on a TV series or call my parents. I try not to look at my laptop after nine, otherwise I struggle to fall asleep.
vocab: làm đầu óc thoải mái, tỉnh táo
xem/làm bù những gì bỏ lỡ

Describe a job that you would like to do.a:
The job I'd really like to do in the future is to become a user experience designer, or UX designer. Basically, it's someone who works out how people interact with apps and websites, and then designs them so they're easy and enjoyable to use.

In terms of skills, it requires quite a broad range. First of all, you need to understand people, so research and interviewing skills are essential. You also need a good eye for visual design and the ability to use tools like Figma. On top of that, communication is crucial, because UX designers have to explain their ideas to developers, managers and clients, and sometimes defend them when people disagree.

As for how I could get this job, I've already taken the first step. Last year, I completed an online course in UX design, and I've started building a portfolio by redesigning a few apps that I personally find frustrating. My plan is to apply for an internship at a tech company after I graduate, so that I can learn from experienced designers. I'm also thinking about doing a master's degree later on, but I'd rather get some hands-on experience first.

The main reason I'd like to do this job is that it combines two things I love: creativity and problem-solving. I got interested in it when I watched my grandmother struggle to use a banking app, and I remember thinking that the design simply wasn't made with people like her in mind. I find it really meaningful that good design can make technology accessible to everyone. Plus, it's a fast-growing field with plenty of opportunities, so it seems like a smart career choice as well.
vocab: có con mắt tinh tường về

Is a high salary more important than job.a: Personally, I'd put job satisfaction first, although I don't think salary should be dismissed. If you dread going to work every morning, no amount of money can really make up for that, and in the long run it can take a toll on your mental health. That said, a decent salary is essential, especially for people supporting a family or living in an expensive city. For a young graduate, for example, financial security might reasonably come first. So I'd say the ideal is a job that pays enough to live comfortably and still gives you a sense of purpose.
vocab: cảm giác có mục đích, ý nghĩa

How will automation affect employment in.a: I think automation will have a mixed effect. In the short term, workers in manufacturing, transport and administration are probably the most at risk, because machines and software can already do many of their tasks faster and more cheaply. That could lead to unemployment in certain regions. In the long run, however, history suggests that new technologies tend to create new kinds of jobs that we can't even imagine yet. The key issue is the transition period. Unless governments and companies invest seriously in retraining, a lot of people could be left behind.
vocab: tác động vừa tốt vừa xấu

Why do some people change careers later.a: There are several reasons, I think. Some people simply realise that the career they chose at twenty doesn't suit who they've become. Others experience burnout after years in a stressful job and want something more balanced. A friend of my father's, for example, left banking in his forties to open a small bakery, because he wanted to do something with his hands. Changes in the economy also play a part, since some industries shrink and force people to retrain. And these days, with online courses so widely available, switching careers seems far less risky than it used to be.

Do you like travelling?.a: Yes, I absolutely love it. For me, travelling is the best way to step out of my comfort zone and see how other people live. I don't need to go anywhere exotic, though. Even a weekend trip to a nearby province can recharge my batteries, especially if I get to try some local food.
vocab: step out of my comfort zone
bước ra khỏi vùng an toàn

Where did you go on your last holiday?.a: My last holiday was a four-day trip to Da Lat with a couple of university friends. It's a hill town in the Central Highlands, so it was a nice escape from the heat. We spent most of our time wandering around flower gardens, sipping coffee in little cafés and exploring the night market.
vocab: một sự trốn chạy dễ chịu khỏi

Do you prefer travelling alone or with f.a: I generally prefer travelling with friends, because sharing experiences makes them more memorable, and it's cheaper when you split the costs. Having said that, I went on a short solo trip last year, and I was surprised by how much I enjoyed the freedom. I could change my plans on a whim without having to consult anyone.

Describe a memorable trip you have taken.a:
I'd like to talk about a trip I took to Hoi An, the ancient town in central Vietnam, about three years ago, right after I finished my final high school exams.

I went with my three closest friends from school. We'd been stuck indoors revising for months, so we promised each other that as soon as the exams were over, we'd go somewhere together to celebrate. We didn't have much money, so we took an overnight train from Hanoi, which was an adventure in itself. We stayed up most of the night chatting and playing cards in our tiny sleeper cabin.

Once we arrived, we spent four days exploring the old town. We rented bicycles and rode through the narrow streets lined with yellow houses, and we spent hours trying street food, especially cao lau and banh mi. One day, we cycled out to An Bang beach, and another day we took a cooking class where we learnt to make spring rolls from scratch. On our last night, during the full-moon festival, we released paper lanterns onto the river and each made a wish.

The reason this trip was so memorable is that it marked the end of an important chapter in our lives. We knew we'd soon be going to different universities in different cities, so there was a bittersweet feeling throughout the trip. I remember sitting by the river on that last night, watching the lanterns float away, and feeling both excited about the future and a bit sad. It was also the first time I'd travelled without my parents, so I felt really independent and grown-up. Even now, whenever the four of us meet up, we always end up reminiscing about that trip.
vocab: bản thân nó đã là một cuộc phiêu lưu
từ đầu, từ nguyên liệu thô
mark the end of an important chapter
đánh dấu sự kết thúc một chương quan trọng
cảm giác vừa vui vừa buồn

What are the benefits of international t.a: The most obvious benefit is economic. Tourism brings in foreign currency and creates jobs, not just in hotels and restaurants, but also for taxi drivers, guides and local craftspeople. In Vietnam, for instance, places like Hoi An have been transformed by tourism. Beyond money, it can also boost a country's international image and encourage the government to preserve historical sites and natural landscapes. There's a cultural benefit too, because contact with visitors can make people more open-minded. Of course, all of this depends on tourism being well managed, otherwise the costs can start to outweigh the gains.
vocab: nâng cao hình ảnh quốc gia

Can tourism damage local culture?.a: I think it certainly can, if it isn't handled carefully. When a place becomes very popular, traditions are sometimes turned into performances just for tourists, and they gradually lose their original meaning. In some villages in the mountains, for example, traditional costumes are now worn mainly for photos rather than in daily life. Rising prices can also push local people out of their own neighbourhoods. That said, tourism can also help keep traditions alive, because it gives communities a financial reason to preserve their crafts and festivals. So it really comes down to how responsibly it's managed.
vocab: mất đi ý nghĩa ban đầu
suy cho cùng phụ thuộc vào

How might travel change in the next twen.a: I imagine travel will become more sustainable, partly out of necessity. As concerns about climate change grow, we might see more people choosing trains over short flights, and airlines may switch to cleaner fuels. Technology will probably make the whole process smoother too, with things like facial recognition replacing passports at airports. It's also possible that virtual reality will let people 'visit' places they can't afford to travel to, although I doubt it will ever replace the real thing. And with popular destinations becoming overcrowded, more governments might limit visitor numbers or introduce tourist taxes.
vocab: vì bắt buộc, vì cần thiết

What do you do to stay healthy?.a: I try to keep things simple. I go for a run three times a week and cycle to class whenever the weather allows. I also make an effort to eat plenty of vegetables and cut back on sugary drinks, which used to be my weakness. And I've realised that getting enough sleep makes a huge difference to my energy levels.

Do you enjoy cooking?.a: Yes, I've really got into it over the past year. When I first moved out of my parents' house, I lived on instant noodles, but I soon got tired of that. Now I enjoy experimenting with simple recipes, especially Vietnamese dishes my mum used to make. Cooking after a long day actually helps me unwind.
vocab: bắt đầu thích, mê điều gì
sống nhờ vào, ăn chủ yếu

How much sleep do you usually get?.a: On weekdays, I usually get around six or seven hours, which is probably a bit less than I need. I tend to stay up late finishing assignments, and then I have early classes. At weekends, I try to catch up on sleep, although I know that isn't the healthiest habit. I'm trying to go to bed earlier.

Describe a healthy habit you would like.a:
One healthy habit I'd really like to develop is waking up early, ideally around half past five, and using that time to exercise and plan my day.

To be honest, I haven't managed to develop this habit yet, mainly because I'm a bit of a night owl. My brain seems to work best late at night, so I often end up studying or scrolling on my phone until after midnight. Then, of course, when my alarm goes off at half five, I just hit the snooze button and go back to sleep. I've tried several times, but I usually give up after a few days, especially when the weather is cold or I've had a stressful week.

As for how I could start, or rather how I plan to start this time, I think the key is to change my evenings first rather than my mornings. I'm going to set a rule that I put my phone away at ten o'clock and leave it charging in the kitchen, so I'm not tempted to check it in bed. I'll also lay out my running clothes the night before, so there are fewer excuses in the morning. And instead of jumping straight to half five, I'll set my alarm fifteen minutes earlier each week, so the change is gradual.

I'm sure this habit would improve my life in several ways. Physically, I'd get regular exercise without it eating into my day. Mentally, I'd start each morning feeling calm and in control, instead of rushing out of the door. Several of my friends who are early risers say they're far more productive, and I'd love to experience that for myself. In the long run, I think it would make me healthier, less stressed and more disciplined overall.
vocab: cú đêm, người hay thức khuya

Why are obesity rates increasing in many.a: I think it's mainly a combination of diet and lifestyle. Processed food and sugary drinks have become cheap and widely available, and they're often marketed very aggressively, especially to children. At the same time, people are far less active than before. Many of us sit at a desk all day, drive or ride motorbikes everywhere, and spend our free time in front of screens. Busy schedules also play a role, because when people are short of time, they tend to rely on fast food rather than cooking. So it isn't simply a matter of individual willpower; the environment we live in matters a great deal.

Should the government tax unhealthy food.a: On balance, I'm in favour of it, particularly for sugary drinks. There's evidence from countries like the UK and Mexico that taxes on soft drinks have reduced consumption and pushed companies to cut the sugar in their products. The money raised could also be spent on healthcare or sports facilities. However, I can see the argument against it. Such taxes may hit low-income families hardest, since they spend a larger share of their income on food. So I think a tax works best when it's combined with making healthy food cheaper and easier to access.
vocab: ảnh hưởng nặng nề nhất đến ai

Is mental health as important as physica.a: Absolutely, and I'd even say the two are closely linked. If someone is suffering from anxiety or depression, it often affects their sleep, their appetite and their ability to work, so their physical health suffers too. The problem is that mental health issues are often invisible, and in many cultures, including mine, people still feel ashamed to talk about them. Fortunately, attitudes are slowly changing, especially among younger people. I think schools and workplaces should treat mental health just as seriously as a broken leg, by offering counselling and encouraging people to seek help early.

How do you usually get the news?.a: Mostly through my phone, to be honest. I follow a couple of reliable news websites, and I glance at the headlines during my morning commute. I also listen to a news podcast while I'm cooking. I rarely buy a newspaper these days, although my dad still reads one every morning with his coffee.
vocab: quãng đường đi làm/học buổi sáng

Do you watch videos online every day?.a: Yes, pretty much every day. I usually watch a few short videos on YouTube while having lunch, often cooking tutorials or travel vlogs. I also use online videos for studying, for example, explanations of tricky grammar points. The only problem is that it's easy to lose track of time, so I try to set myself a limit.

Do you trust the information you read on.a: Not really, or at least not straight away. There's so much misleading content out there that I've learned to take everything with a pinch of salt. If I see a shocking story, I usually check whether a reputable news outlet has reported it before I believe it, and I definitely don't share it until I've double-checked.
vocab: take something with a pinch of salt
không hoàn toàn tin điều gì
cơ quan báo chí uy tín

Describe an advertisement that you remem.a:
The advertisement I remember best is a TV commercial for a brand of instant coffee that came out a few years ago, around the Lunar New Year.

I first saw it on television at my grandparents' house, during the week before Tet, and then it was everywhere, on YouTube, on Facebook and even on big screens at bus stops. I think I must have watched it dozens of times without getting bored, which is quite unusual for an advert.

What was clever about it was that it barely showed the product at all. Instead, it told a short story about a young man who had moved to the city for work and hadn't been home for several years. He was always too busy, always promising his elderly father that he'd visit next time. In the advert, he finally takes the long bus journey back to his village on New Year's Eve, and his father, who had been waiting by the gate, makes him a cup of coffee. There was hardly any dialogue, just gentle music and the sound of rain. Only at the very end did the brand's logo appear, with a short line about coming home.

The main reason I remember it is that it struck a chord with me personally. At the time, I'd just started university in another city, and I was feeling quite homesick. I remember my eyes welling up the first time I saw it, and I immediately called my parents afterwards. I think it was a brilliant example of emotional advertising, because instead of telling people to buy coffee, it connected the brand with family and nostalgia. To be honest, I still associate that brand with going home for Tet.
vocab: chạm đến cảm xúc của ai

Should advertising aimed at children be.a: Yes, I strongly believe it should be. Young children aren't able to tell the difference between entertainment and a sales pitch, so they're easily persuaded by colourful characters and catchy songs. This is especially worrying when it comes to junk food and toys, because children then pester their parents for things they don't need. Some countries, like Sweden, have already banned TV adverts aimed at under-twelves. Of course, it's much harder to regulate online, since adverts are often disguised as videos by influencers. But I think stricter rules, along with teaching children media literacy, would make a real difference.
vocab: nằng nặc đòi ai thứ gì

How can people recognise fake news?.a: I think the first step is simply to slow down. Fake news is often designed to provoke a strong emotional reaction, so if a headline makes you angry or shocked, that's a warning sign. People should also check the source: is it a well-known news outlet, or a website they've never heard of? Another useful habit is cross-checking, which means seeing whether other reliable sources are reporting the same story. With images, a reverse image search can reveal whether a photo is old or taken out of context. Ultimately, though, I believe schools need to teach these skills from an early age.

Will newspapers disappear in the future?.a: Printed newspapers will probably become much rarer, but I don't think they'll vanish completely. Most young people already get their news online, and printing and distributing paper is expensive, so many publications have cut back on their print editions or gone fully digital. However, there will likely remain a niche market of older readers and people who simply enjoy the ritual of reading a paper over breakfast. More importantly, I think newspapers as organisations will survive, because we'll always need professional journalists. They'll just reach us through apps and websites rather than on paper.
vocab: chuyển hoàn toàn sang kỹ thuật số
thói quen, nghi thức (hằng ngày) của việc

Where is your hometown?.a: My hometown is Nam Dinh, a small city about ninety kilometres south of Hanoi. It's not a famous tourist destination, but it's known for its textile industry and for a delicious type of noodle soup. It's quite peaceful compared with Hanoi, and life there moves at a much gentler pace.
vocab: với nhịp độ nhẹ nhàng hơn

What do you like most about the place wh.a: What I like most is the sense of community. I live in a small alley in Hanoi, and the neighbours all know each other. In the evenings, people sit outside chatting, and the older ladies always keep an eye on the children playing. It feels much friendlier than living in a big apartment block where nobody says hello.

How do you usually travel around your ci.a: Like most people in Vietnam, I mainly get around by motorbike, because it's fast and convenient for weaving through traffic. For longer journeys across the city, I sometimes use ride-hailing apps. Recently, I've started taking the new metro line now and then, which is surprisingly comfortable, and it means I can read on the way.

Describe a city you would like to live i.a:
The city I'd love to live in one day is Melbourne, in the south-east of Australia.

I first got to know about it through my older cousin, who moved there to do a master's degree about five years ago and has stayed on to work. She's always sending me photos and telling me stories about her life there, and I've also watched quite a few travel vlogs and documentaries about it. Melbourne is regularly ranked as one of the world's most liveable cities, so I suppose that caught my attention as well.

From what I've seen and heard, it's a really vibrant and multicultural city. It's famous for its coffee culture, with tiny cafés tucked away in narrow lanes covered in street art. There are also lots of green spaces, like the Royal Botanic Gardens, and the beach isn't far from the city centre. Public transport seems excellent too, especially the trams, which are free in the central area. And from what my cousin says, there's always something going on, whether it's a food festival, a live music event or a big sporting match.

The main reason I'd like to live there is that it seems to offer a great balance between work and lifestyle. As someone who wants to work in marketing, I'd have plenty of career opportunities, but I'd also be able to enjoy nature and a relaxed pace of life at weekends. I really like the idea of a city where people from so many different backgrounds live side by side, because I think it would broaden my horizons. Of course, I know it's expensive and the weather can be unpredictable, but I'd definitely like to give it a try for a few years.
vocab: những thành phố đáng sống nhất

What are the main problems of living in.a: I'd say the most obvious problems are traffic congestion and pollution. In cities like Hanoi, people can spend hours every day stuck in traffic, breathing in exhaust fumes. Another major issue is the cost of living, especially housing, which forces many young people to live in cramped rooms far from their workplace. Big cities can also be surprisingly lonely, since people are often too busy to get to know their neighbours. Having said that, these problems exist precisely because cities offer so many opportunities, so it's really about managing growth better rather than avoiding cities altogether.

How can governments reduce traffic conge.a: I think the most effective long-term solution is to invest heavily in public transport, so it becomes a genuinely attractive alternative to private vehicles. Metro systems and dedicated bus lanes, for example, can move huge numbers of people quickly. At the same time, governments could discourage driving in city centres, perhaps through congestion charges, as London has done. Better urban planning also matters. If schools, offices and shops are spread more evenly, people won't all need to travel to the same area at rush hour. None of these measures is a quick fix, but together they could make a real difference.
vocab: một lựa chọn thay thế thật sự hấp dẫn

Why do young people move from the countr.a: The main reason is undoubtedly opportunity. Most universities, well-paid jobs and big companies are concentrated in cities, so young people often feel they have no choice but to move if they want to get ahead. Cities also offer a more exciting lifestyle, with better entertainment, shopping and nightlife. In my own village, for example, nearly all of my cousins have moved to Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City for work. However, I think this trend could slow down a little in the future, as remote working becomes more common and rural areas get better infrastructure.
vocab: không còn lựa chọn nào khác ngoài

lessons.title: Nguyên âm dài /iː/
lessons.how: Lưỡi nâng cao ở phía trước, đầu lưỡi chạm nhẹ răng dưới. Môi kéo sang hai bên như đang cười, hàm gần khép. Giữ âm dài và căng.
lessons.vn: Người Việt hay đọc ngắn như "i" nên "sheep" nghe thành "ship". Hãy kéo dài gấp đôi và giữ môi căng đến hết âm.
lessons.tip: Giống "i" trong "đi" nhưng kéo dài như khi nói "iii" lúc chụp ảnh.
sentences: Please leave the keys on the seat.
We need three people to agree on each team.

lessons.title: Nguyên âm ngắn /ɪ/
lessons.how: Lưỡi cao và ở phía trước nhưng thấp và lùi hơn /iː/ một chút. Môi thả lỏng, hơi mở. Âm ngắn, dứt khoát.
lessons.vn: Dễ bị đọc thành "i" căng của tiếng Việt hoặc kéo dài. Thả lỏng cơ miệng, âm hơi ngả về "ê" và cắt ngắn.
lessons.tip: Nằm giữa "i" và "ê" của tiếng Việt, nói nhanh và lỏng miệng.
sentences: This big city is busy with visitors.
Did Jim finish his English quiz in six minutes?

lessons.title: Nguyên âm ngắn /e/
lessons.how: Lưỡi ở phía trước, độ cao trung bình. Môi hơi kéo ngang, hàm mở vừa phải. Âm ngắn.
lessons.vn: Thường bị lẫn với /æ/ (pen – pan). Với /e/ hàm chỉ mở vừa, không hạ sâu như /æ/.
lessons.tip: Gần với "e" trong "xe" nhưng ngắn và hơi khép hơn.
sentences: My friend Ben said the test went well.
Getting enough rest helps your health and memory.

lessons.title: Nguyên âm ngắn /æ/
lessons.how: Hạ hàm xuống rõ rệt, lưỡi thấp và nằm phía trước, môi kéo ngang. Âm ngắn, nghe như lai giữa "e" và "a".
lessons.vn: Hay đọc thành "e" hoặc "a" thuần Việt. Hãy mở miệng như định nói "a" nhưng giữ khẩu hình "e".
lessons.tip: Nói "e" rồi hạ cằm xuống thật thấp mà không đổi lưỡi.
sentences: The black cat sat on Dan's mat.
Pack a map and a snack for the traffic jam.

lessons.title: Nguyên âm dài /ɑː/
lessons.how: Mở miệng rộng, lưỡi thấp và lùi về sau. Môi thả lỏng, không tròn. Kéo dài âm. Trong giọng Anh, chữ r sau nó không đọc.
lessons.vn: Hay đọc ngắn như "a" hoặc cố uốn chữ r (car → "ca-rờ"). Giữ âm dài và bỏ r ở cuối.
lessons.tip: Như "a" khi bác sĩ bảo "há miệng ra", kéo dài và sâu trong họng.
sentences: Park the car far from the market.
My father started a large art class.

lessons.title: Nguyên âm ngắn /ɒ/
lessons.how: Lưỡi thấp và lùi sau, hàm mở khá rộng, môi hơi tròn nhẹ. Âm ngắn. Đây là âm đặc trưng của giọng Anh (giọng Mỹ thường đọc thành "a").
lessons.vn: Hay đọc thành "o" căng của tiếng Việt hoặc kéo dài thành /ɔː/. Giữ ngắn và mở hàm nhiều hơn.
lessons.tip: Giữa "o" và "a": nói "o" ngắn nhưng há miệng to hơn.
sentences: Tom often got a hot coffee from the shop.
The top problem is the cost of the job.

lessons.title: Âm /θ/ và /ð/ – không phải “th” tiếng Việt
lessons.how: Cả /θ/ và /ð/ đều là âm “giữa hai răng”: đặt đầu lưỡi nhẹ giữa răng trên và răng dưới (hoặc chạm mặt sau răng trên), rồi thổi hơi qua khe hẹp. /θ/ vô thanh – chỉ có hơi (think, health). /ð/ hữu thanh – có rung dây thanh (the, weather). Đây là âm xát kéo dài được, khác hẳn “th” tiếng Việt (một âm tắc bật hơi).
lessons.howEn: English dental fricatives /θ/ (voiceless: think, three) and /ð/ (voiced: this, weather) are produced by resting the tip of the tongue gently between the front teeth (or behind the upper incisors) and pushing a continuous airstream through the constriction without stopping. Unlike Vietnamese “th”, which is an aspirated stop, they are fricatives: the air keeps flowing.

rules.label: /θ/ vô thanh
rules.when: thường ở từ nội dung: danh từ, động từ, số đếm

rules.label: /ð/ hữu thanh
rules.when: thường ở từ chức năng (the, this, that, they, than) và giữa hai nguyên âm

rules.label: Danh từ /θ/ → động từ /ð/
rules.when: một số cặp đổi âm khi thành động từ

lessons.vn: Người Việt hay đọc /θ/ thành “th” tiếng Việt hoặc /t/ (“think” → “tink”), hoặc /s/ (“think” → “sink”); đọc /ð/ thành /d/ hoặc /z/ (“they” → “day”, “clothing” → “closing”). Cách sửa: soi gương – phải thấy đầu lưỡi lộ ra giữa hai hàm răng; giữ âm kéo dài “θθθθ” vài giây trước khi nói cả từ.
lessons.tip: Thần chú: “Lè lưỡi – thổi hơi.” Nếu không kéo dài được âm thì bạn đang đọc /t/ hoặc /d/, chưa phải /θ/ /ð/.
lessons.tipEn: Tip: Put the tongue tip lightly between the teeth and let the air flow. If the sound stops like a click, you are saying /t/ or /d/ instead of /θ/ or /ð/.
sentences: I think the growth of the city threatens our health.
Although the weather is warm, they rarely go there.
There are three main methods that I would mention.

quiz.explain: “think” /θɪŋk/ bắt đầu bằng /θ/ vô thanh, lưỡi giữa hai răng, chỉ thổi hơi.
“bathe” /beɪð/ là động từ, kết thúc bằng /ð/. “bath” và “path” kết thúc bằng /θ/.

quiz.q: Nếu đọc /ð/ thành /z/, “clothing” sẽ nghe giống từ nào?
Âm /θ/ khác “th” tiếng Việt ở điểm nào?
options: /θ/ là âm xát, kéo dài được
quiz.explain: “th” tiếng Việt là âm tắc bật hơi. /θ/ là âm xát: hơi đi qua khe giữa lưỡi và răng, có thể kéo dài.

quiz.q: “the” trong câu thường đọc là gì trước phụ âm?
quiz.explain: Trước phụ âm, “the” là dạng yếu /ðə/. Trước nguyên âm thường là /ði/. /də/ là lỗi thay /ð/ bằng /d/.

lessons.title: Trọng âm câu và dạng yếu
lessons.how: Tiếng Anh có nhịp dựa trên trọng âm: các từ mang nội dung (danh từ, động từ chính, tính từ, trạng từ, từ phủ định, từ để hỏi) được nhấn; các từ chức năng (giới từ, mạo từ, trợ động từ, đại từ, liên từ) thường đọc nhanh và nhẹ với nguyên âm /ə/ – gọi là dạng yếu. Khoảng cách giữa các từ được nhấn gần như đều nhau, nên các từ yếu bị “nén” lại.
lessons.howEn: In natural spoken English, content words (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs), negatives and question words receive sentence stress, while grammatical function words (articles, prepositions, auxiliaries, pronouns, conjunctions) are often reduced to weak forms with /ə/ in the middle of a sentence. Stressed words tend to fall at fairly regular intervals, so weak words are squeezed between them. Function words keep strong forms at the end of a clause, when stressed for contrast, and negatives such as can’t are separate words with a full vowel (UK /kɑːnt/, US /kænt/). Saying every word with a full vowel makes speech sound stiff and robotic.

rules.label: Từ được nhấn
rules.when: danh từ, động từ chính, tính từ, trạng từ, not/never, từ để hỏi

rules.label: Dạng yếu
rules.when: giới từ, mạo từ, trợ động từ, liên từ khi đứng giữa câu

rules.label: Dạng mạnh
rules.when: khi đứng cuối câu, khi được nhấn đối lập, hoặc phủ định

lessons.vn: Người Việt đọc mọi từ to và rõ như nhau (“I – WANT – TO – GO – TO – THE – PARK”), làm câu nghe “cứng như robot” và giám khảo khó nhận ra từ khóa. Đặc biệt nguy hiểm: “can” đọc mạnh /kæn/ dễ bị nghe thành “can't”. Cách sửa: gạch chân từ nội dung, đọc to chúng trước, sau đó “chèn” các từ yếu vào giữa thật nhanh mà giữ nguyên nhịp.
lessons.tip: Thần chú: “Nội dung thì nhấn – chức năng thì lướt.” Trong giọng Anh, “can” khẳng định là /kən/, còn “can't” là /kɑːnt/ – nguyên âm dài khác hẳn.
lessons.tipEn: Tip: Stress the content, glide over the grammar. Positive “can” is usually /kən/, whereas “can’t” keeps a full vowel: /kɑːnt/ in British English, /kænt/ in American English.
sentences: I WANT to GO to the PARK. ↘
PEOple can SAVE a LOT of MONey by COOKing at HOME. ↘
MOST of my FRIENDS are INterested in TECHnology. ↘

quiz.q: Trong “a cup of tea”, “of” thường đọc là?
quiz.explain: Giữa câu, “of” là dạng yếu /əv/, nói nhanh có thể chỉ còn /ə/: /ə ˈkʌp ə ˈtiː/.

quiz.q: Từ nào thường ĐƯỢC NHẤN trong câu?
quiz.explain: “pollution” là danh từ – từ nội dung. “the” và “and” là từ chức năng, thường đọc yếu.

quiz.q: Câu “I can swim” trong giọng Anh, “can” đọc là?
quiz.explain: Khẳng định, giữa câu → /kən/, và nhấn vào “SWIM”. “can't” mới là /kɑːnt/.

options: Ở cuối câu: “Where are you from?”
quiz.explain: Giới từ đứng cuối câu dùng dạng mạnh. Giữa câu (“I come from Hanoi”) là /frəm/.

th-s: Thè đầu lưỡi ra giữa hai hàm răng rồi thổi hơi nhẹ – không để lưỡi sau răng.
Giữ đầu lưỡi sau răng trên, không thè ra; xì hơi như tiếng rắn “sss”.
th-t: Thè đầu lưỡi ra giữa hai hàm răng rồi thổi hơi nhẹ – không để lưỡi sau răng.
Chạm đầu lưỡi vào lợi sau răng trên rồi bật ra – không thè lưỡi.
dh-d: Thè đầu lưỡi giữa hai hàm răng, thổi hơi và rung cổ (đặt tay lên cổ để cảm nhận).
Đầu lưỡi chạm lợi sau răng trên rồi bật ra, có rung cổ – không thè lưỡi.
dh-z: Thè đầu lưỡi giữa hai hàm răng, thổi hơi và rung cổ (đặt tay lên cổ để cảm nhận).
Giữ lưỡi sau răng và ngân “zzz” như tiếng ong – không thè lưỡi.
s-z: Âm cuối /s/ không rung cổ và nguyên âm trước nó ngắn: “rice” gọn, xì hơi rõ.
Âm cuối /z/ rung cổ và kéo dài nguyên âm trước nó: “riiise-zzz”.
final-drop: Đừng nuốt âm cuối: chặn rồi bật nhẹ /t/, /k/, /p/, /d/ ở cuối từ.
Từ này kết thúc bằng nguyên âm – không thêm phụ âm cuối, kéo dài nguyên âm tự nhiên.
final-voice: Phụ âm cuối vô thanh: cắt nguyên âm ngắn rồi bật hơi gọn /t/ /k/ /f/.
Phụ âm cuối hữu thanh: kéo dài nguyên âm và rung cổ khi kết thúc /d/ /ɡ/ /v/.
p-b: Cuối từ /p/: khép môi, nguyên âm ngắn, bật hơi nhẹ – không rung cổ.
Cuối từ /b/: nguyên âm dài hơn, khép môi và rung cổ – đừng đọc thành “p”.
plural: Từ này ở dạng số ít – dừng sau phụ âm cuối, không thêm /s/.
Đừng bỏ đuôi -s: đọc rõ /s/, /z/ hoặc /ɪz/ ở cuối từ.
ed: Đây là dạng nguyên mẫu – kết thúc gọn, không thêm âm /t/ hay /d/.
Đọc rõ đuôi -ed: /t/ sau âm vô thanh, /d/ sau âm hữu thanh, /ɪd/ sau t, d.
sh-s: Chu môi tròn ra trước, lưỡi lùi về sau một chút, thổi “suỵt” /ʃ/.
Môi dẹt, đầu lưỡi sát răng trên, xì hơi mảnh “sss” – không chu môi.
ch-sh: Bắt đầu bằng một cú chặn /t/ rồi bật ra “ch” – âm ngắn, dứt khoát.
Không chặn lưỡi: để hơi chảy liên tục “shhh”.
ch-j: Như “ch” nhưng không rung cổ – chỉ bật hơi.
Cùng khẩu hình với “ch” nhưng rung cổ: “j” trong “jeep”.
j-z: Chặn lưỡi rồi bật ra “dʒ” có rung cổ – môi hơi chu.
Không chặn: lưỡi sau răng, ngân liên tục “zzz”.
j-y: Âm “j” có chặn lưỡi và rung cổ, mạnh hơn “y”.
Âm /j/ nhẹ, lướt nhanh như “i” ngắn – lưỡi không chạm ngạc.
r-l: Cong đầu lưỡi lên nhưng KHÔNG chạm ngạc, môi hơi tròn.
Đầu lưỡi chạm chắc vào lợi sau răng trên, hơi đi hai bên lưỡi.
l-n: Đầu lưỡi chạm lợi nhưng hơi đi qua miệng – không phải qua mũi.
Đầu lưỡi chạm lợi và hơi đi qua mũi (bịt mũi sẽ thấy khác).
cluster: Đọc liền cụm phụ âm, không chèn “ơ” vào giữa: “sport”, không phải “sơ-port”.
Từ này có thêm một âm tiết nhẹ /ə/ – đọc rõ hai âm tiết.
i-ih: Kéo môi cười, căng lưỡi và kéo dài “iiii”.
Thả lỏng miệng, đọc ngắn và gọn – giữa “i” và “ê”.
ae-e: Há miệng rộng, hạ cằm xuống thấp như “e” kéo về “a”.
Miệng mở vừa, cằm không hạ sâu – “e” gọn.
uh-ah: Miệng mở vừa, thả lỏng, âm ngắn như “â”.
Há miệng thật to, lưỡi hạ thấp, kéo dài “aaa” như khi bác sĩ khám họng.
v-b: Răng trên chạm nhẹ môi dưới, thổi hơi và rung cổ – môi không khép lại.
Hai môi khép chặt rồi bật ra – răng không chạm môi.
w-v: Chu tròn hai môi như “u” rồi mở ra – răng không chạm môi.
Răng trên chạm môi dưới, rung cổ “vvv” – không tròn môi.

scripts.title: Meeting a new neighbour

ai.name: Emma
ai.persona: warm, friendly and patient, speaks slowly and clearly
ai.goal: get to know the learner and invite them for a coffee

scripts.you: Say hello, introduce yourself, say where you are from and what you do, and agree to meet again.
scripts.cando: Chào hỏi, giới thiệu bản thân và hỏi thăm người mới quen
vocab: in the house or flat beside yours
a person who lives near you
start living in a new home
a question about someone's country or city
at a time in the future that is not fixed

a: Hi! I'm Emma. I live next door.
Hi there! I'm Emma – I just moved in next door.
Hi! I'm Emma – I've just moved in next door, actually.
h: Hi Emma! I'm Sam. Nice to meet you.
Hi Emma, nice to meet you! I'm Sam.
Oh hi, Emma! Lovely to meet you – I'm Sam.
turns.tip: Chào lại và nói tên của bạn

a: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
Nice to meet you too. So, where are you from?
Nice to meet you too! So where are you from originally?
h: I'm from Brazil.
I'm from Brazil, from a city near Rio. How about you?
I'm from Brazil originally, but I've lived here for two years now. How about you?
turns.tip: Nói bạn đến từ đâu

a: Oh, nice! What do you do?
Oh, nice! And what do you do?
Oh, how lovely! And what do you do?
h: I'm a student. I study English.
I'm a student. I study business at the university.
I'm studying business at the university, and I work part-time in a café.
turns.tip: Nói về công việc hoặc việc học của bạn

a: Do you like it here?
Do you like living here?
So, how do you like living around here?
h: Yes, I like it. It's quiet.
Yes, I really like it. It's quiet and the people are friendly.
I love it – it's quiet, but there are lots of nice cafés nearby.
turns.tip: Nói bạn có thích nơi này không và vì sao

a: Me too. Do you want a coffee some time?
Me too. Would you like to have a coffee some time?
Same here. We should get a coffee some time – are you free this weekend?
h: Yes, thank you! Saturday is good for me.
I'd love to! Are you free on Saturday?
That sounds great! Saturday morning works for me, if that suits you.
turns.tip: Nhận lời mời và gợi ý một ngày

end: Great. See you on Saturday. Bye!
Perfect – see you on Saturday. Bye!
Perfect, see you on Saturday then. Have a nice evening!

scripts.title: Ordering at a café

ai.name: Tom
ai.persona: cheerful and quick, but kind to people who are learning English
ai.goal: take the learner's order and payment

scripts.you: Order a drink and something to eat, choose the size, say if it is for here or to go, and pay.
scripts.cando: Gọi đồ uống, chọn cỡ ly và thanh toán ở quán cà phê
vocab: coffee with a lot of hot milk
you will eat or drink in the café
you will take it with you
the long table where you order and pay

a: Hi! What can I get you?
Hi there! What can I get for you?
Morning! What can I get you today?
h: A coffee, please.
Can I have a latte, please?
Could I get a medium latte with oat milk, please?
turns.tip: Gọi đồ uống, nhớ nói "please"

a: Small or large?
Sure. Small, medium or large?
Sure thing. What size would you like?
h: Large, please.
Medium, please.
A medium, please – not too hot, if possible.
turns.tip: Chọn cỡ ly

a: For here or to go?
Is that for here or to go?
Are you having that here or taking it away?
h: For here, please.
For here, please. And can I have a croissant too?
I'll have it here, thanks. Could I also get a croissant?
turns.tip: Nói uống tại quán hay mang đi; có thể gọi thêm đồ ăn
br: Okay, I'll put a lid on it.

a: That's five pounds fifty. Cash or card?
That comes to five fifty. Cash or card?
That'll be five pounds fifty altogether. Are you paying by card?
h: Card, please.
Card, please. Here you are.
Yes, by card, please – can I just tap?
turns.tip: Chọn trả bằng tiền mặt hay thẻ

a: Thank you. Your name, please?
Thanks! Can I get a name for the order?
Lovely. And what name shall I put on the cup?
h: My name is Sam.
It's Sam. S-A-M.
It's Sam – S, A, M. Thanks very much!
turns.tip: Nói tên và đánh vần nếu cần

end: Thank you, Sam. It's ready in two minutes.
Thanks, Sam! It'll be ready in two minutes.
Thanks, Sam – it'll be ready at the end of the counter in a couple of minutes.

scripts.title: Buying clothes in a shop

ai.name: Mia
ai.role: shop assistant in a clothes shop
ai.goal: help the learner find the right T-shirt and sell it

scripts.you: Ask for a T-shirt, say your size and colour, try it on, say how it fits, and pay.
scripts.cando: Hỏi cỡ, màu, thử đồ và mua hàng ở cửa hàng quần áo
vocab: put on clothes to see if they are right
a small room in a shop where you try on clothes
a paper that shows what you paid
red, blue, green and so on

a: Hello! Can I help you?
Hi! Can I help you with anything?
Hi there! Are you looking for anything in particular?
h: Yes, please. I want a T-shirt.
Yes, please. I'm looking for a T-shirt.
Yes, actually – I'm looking for a plain T-shirt for work.
turns.tip: Nói món đồ bạn muốn mua

a: What size are you?
Sure. What size are you?
Of course. What size do you usually take?
h: Medium, please.
I'm a medium, I think.
Usually a medium, but it depends on the brand.
turns.tip: Nói cỡ của bạn (S, M, L…)

a: What colour do you like?
We have white, black and blue. Which colour would you like?
It comes in white, black and navy. Do you have a colour in mind?
h: Blue, please. Can I try it?
Could I try the blue one, please?
I'd like to try the navy one, please. Where are the changing rooms?
turns.tip: Chọn màu và xin thử đồ

a: Here you are. How is it?
Here you go. How does it fit?
There you go. So, how does it fit?
h: It's good. I like it.
It fits well. I really like it.
It fits perfectly, actually. I like the colour too.
turns.tip: Nói đồ vừa hay không vừa
br: Oh, let me get you another size.
Great, it looks good on you.

a: It's twenty pounds. Is that OK?
It's twenty pounds. Would you like to buy it?
It's twenty pounds, and they're half price if you buy two today. Would you like to take it?
h: Yes, please. Here is my card.
Yes, I'll take it, please. Can I pay by card?
Yes, I'll take it, thanks. Just the one for now – can I pay by card?
turns.tip: Đồng ý mua và hỏi cách thanh toán

end: Yes. Thank you! Have a nice day.
Of course. Here's your receipt – have a nice day!
Of course. Here's your receipt – you can return it within thirty days. Have a lovely day!

scripts.title: Asking for directions

ai.name: Ben
ai.role: a local person in the street
ai.persona: kind and patient, gives simple directions
ai.goal: help the learner find the train station

scripts.you: Ask the way to the station, check the directions, ask how far it is, and say thank you.
scripts.cando: Hỏi đường, hiểu chỉ dẫn đơn giản (đi thẳng, rẽ trái/phải) và cảm ơn
vocab: go to the left at a corner
on the right side of you

a: Hi. Are you OK?
Hi – are you lost? Can I help?
Hi there, you look a bit lost. Can I help at all?
h: Excuse me. Where is the train station?
Yes, please. How do I get to the train station?
Yes, please! Could you tell me the way to the train station?
turns.tip: Mở lời lịch sự ("Excuse me") và hỏi đường tới nơi bạn cần

a: Go straight on. Then turn left.
Sure. Go straight on and take the second left.
Sure. Go straight down this road and take the second turning on the left.
h: Straight on, then left. OK.
So straight on, then the second left?
So straight on, and then the second left – got it.
turns.tip: Nhắc lại chỉ dẫn để chắc mình hiểu đúng

a: Yes. The station is on the right.
That's right. Then the station is on your right, next to the bank.
Exactly. Then you'll see the station on your right, just past the bank.
h: Is it far?
Is it far from here?
Is it far? Should I take a bus?
turns.tip: Hỏi đường có xa không

a: No. Ten minutes on foot.
No, it's about ten minutes on foot.
Not really – it's about a ten-minute walk, so you don't need the bus.
h: Great. Thank you very much!
Great, thank you so much for your help!
Perfect – thanks so much, that's really kind of you.
turns.tip: Cảm ơn người đã giúp bạn

a: You're welcome. Where are you going?
No problem. Where are you going today?
No problem at all. Where are you heading?
h: I'm going to London.
I'm going to London to see a friend.
I'm heading to London to visit a friend for the weekend.
turns.tip: Nói bạn đi đâu và để làm gì

end: Lovely – enjoy your weekend in London!

scripts.title: Checking in at a hotel

ai.name: Sofia
ai.goal: check the learner in and answer their questions

scripts.you: Check in with your reservation, show your passport, confirm your booking, and ask about breakfast, Wi-Fi and check-out.
scripts.cando: Nhận phòng khách sạn: nói tên đặt phòng, hỏi giờ ăn sáng, Wi-Fi và giờ trả phòng
vocab: a room you booked before you arrived
arrive at a hotel and get your key
a room for two people with one big bed
a plastic card that opens your room

a: Good evening. Welcome to the Park Hotel.
Good evening, welcome to the Park Hotel. How can I help?
Good evening and welcome to the Park Hotel. Are you checking in?
h: Hello. I have a room. My name is Sam Lee.
Hi, I have a reservation. My name is Sam Lee.
Good evening. Yes, I have a reservation under the name Sam Lee.
turns.tip: Nói bạn đã đặt phòng và cho biết tên

a: Thank you. Your passport, please.
Thank you. Can I see your passport, please?
Lovely, thank you. Could I see your passport or ID, please?
h: Here you are.
Sure, here you are.
Of course – here you go.
turns.tip: Đưa giấy tờ và nói "Here you are"

a: You have a double room for two nights.
So, that's a double room for two nights, until Friday.
Right, I can see a double room for two nights, checking out on Friday. Is that correct?
h: Yes. What time is breakfast?
Yes, that's right. What time is breakfast?
Yes, that's correct. Is breakfast included, and what time is it served?
turns.tip: Xác nhận đặt phòng và hỏi giờ ăn sáng

a: Breakfast is from seven to ten.
Breakfast is from seven to ten in the restaurant.
Breakfast is included – it's served from seven till ten in the restaurant on the ground floor.
h: Thank you. Is there Wi-Fi?
Great. And is there Wi-Fi in the room?
Great. And what's the Wi-Fi password, please?
turns.tip: Hỏi về Wi-Fi hoặc dịch vụ khác

a: Yes. The password is on your key card. Your room is 305.
Yes, the password is on your key card. You're in room 305, on the third floor.
The password is on the back of your key card. You're in room 305 on the third floor – the lifts are just behind you.
h: Thank you. What time is check-out?
Thank you. What time is check-out?
Perfect, thanks. And what time is check-out on Friday?
turns.tip: Cảm ơn và hỏi giờ trả phòng

end: Check-out is at eleven. Have a nice stay!
Check-out is at eleven. Enjoy your stay!
Check-out is at eleven. If you need anything, just call reception. Enjoy your stay!

scripts.title: At the doctor's

ai.name: Dr Patel
ai.persona: calm, kind, asks simple questions one at a time
ai.goal: understand the learner's symptoms and give simple advice

scripts.you: Describe your symptoms, say when they started, answer the doctor's questions, and ask how long it will take to get better.
scripts.cando: Nói triệu chứng và thời gian bị bệnh với bác sĩ, hiểu lời khuyên đơn giản
vocab: body heat that is higher than normal
something you take to get better
a common illness with a runny nose and a cough

a: Hello. Please sit down. What's the problem?
Hello, please take a seat. What seems to be the problem?
Hello, come in and have a seat. So, what brings you in today?
h: I'm ill. I have a headache.
I don't feel well. I have a bad headache and a sore throat.
I haven't been feeling well. I've got a bad headache and a sore throat.
turns.tip: Nói bạn bị đau ở đâu ("I have a headache")

a: When did it start?
I'm sorry to hear that. When did it start?
Oh dear. How long have you had these symptoms?
h: Two days ago.
It started two days ago.
For about two days now – it started on Monday evening.
turns.tip: Nói bệnh bắt đầu từ khi nào

a: Do you have a temperature?
I see. Do you have a temperature?
Right. Have you had a temperature at all?
h: Yes, a little.
Yes, I think so. I feel hot and tired.
Yes, a slight one – I've been feeling hot and really tired.
turns.tip: Trả lời có sốt không và bạn thấy thế nào

a: Do you take any medicine?
Are you taking any medicine at the moment?
Are you taking anything for it at the moment?
h: No, I don't.
Just some paracetamol for the headache.
Only some paracetamol for the headache, but it doesn't help much.
turns.tip: Nói bạn có đang uống thuốc gì không

a: OK. It's a cold. Rest and drink water.
It looks like a cold. Rest, drink lots of water, and you can take paracetamol.
It looks like a virus, so antibiotics won't help. Get plenty of rest, drink lots of fluids and keep taking paracetamol.
h: OK. How many days?
Okay. How long will it take to get better?
Okay, thank you. How long should it take to clear up?
turns.tip: Hỏi bao lâu thì khỏi

end: About one week. Come back if it gets worse. Get well soon!
About a week. Come back if you don't feel better. Get well soon!
Usually about a week. If it gets worse, or you're not better in ten days, come back and see me. Get well soon!
